items.prompt: In a IoT command delivery system, a device control plane must send a command to a device. duplicate delivery must not cause an unsafe repeated action The design review focuses on rate limits, quotas, fairness, and overload signaling. The normal path is healthy and the design must show where the decision belongs. What is the best primary architecture decision?
constraints: duplicate delivery must not cause an unsafe repeated action
Choose the mechanism that directly satisfies the stated contract before adding adjacent controls.
The primary decision is enforce quotas and overload signaling at the boundary that can identify caller and resource cost..
Keep the scenario provider-neutral and do not rely on a canonical product solution.

options.text: Enforce quotas and overload signaling at the boundary that can identify caller and resource cost. In this normal path for IoT command delivery, fairness requires an attributable budget and an explicit response when capacity is unavailable. The owner must also make a reconnecting device replaying a command observable rather than silently passing it to another layer.
Choose the nearest familiar component and let each caller decide rate limits, quotas, fairness, and overload signaling independently, without a shared owner or failure contract.
Add replication, caching, retries, or asynchronous buffering immediately, even though the scenario has not shown that mechanism is the limiting constraint.
Keep the happy path and treat a reconnecting device replaying a command as an operational exception that the caller can resolve manually.
Select a named cloud or vendor product first and infer the workload, ownership, and guarantee from that product's defaults.

feedback.Reason: Enforce quotas and overload signaling at the boundary that can identify caller and resource cost. It addresses duplicate delivery must not cause an unsafe repeated action through an explicit mechanism and keeps a reconnecting device replaying a command inside a visible ownership and recovery boundary.

Details.errorCorrection: The distractors either make the boundary unowned, add unmeasured complexity, ignore recovery, or replace mechanism reasoning with provider trivia. Choose the mechanism that directly satisfies the stated contract before adding adjacent controls.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Do not reduce “Rate limits, quotas, fairness, and overload signaling” to terminology recall. Distinguish protocol mechanics from domain boundaries; a fashionable API style is not automatically the correct contract. The trade-off is that explicit ownership and evidence may require a narrower contract or an operational signal, but that cost is preferable to silently violating the stated guarantee.

items.prompt: In a financial reporting system, a reporting reader must read a period total. the report must state its freshness and use a consistent cutoff The design review focuses on rate limits, quotas, fairness, and overload signaling. The same mechanism appears in a different domain with one constraint changed. What is the best primary architecture decision?
constraints: the report must state its freshness and use a consistent cutoff
Transfer the ownership and failure rule, then re-evaluate the changed workload rather than copying a product solution.
The primary decision is enforce quotas and overload signaling at the boundary that can identify caller and resource cost..
Keep the scenario provider-neutral and do not rely on a canonical product solution.

options.text: Enforce quotas and overload signaling at the boundary that can identify caller and resource cost. In this transfer case for financial reporting, fairness requires an attributable budget and an explicit response when capacity is unavailable. The owner must also make a read across mixed snapshots observable rather than silently passing it to another layer.
Choose the nearest familiar component and let each caller decide rate limits, quotas, fairness, and overload signaling independently, without a shared owner or failure contract.
Add replication, caching, retries, or asynchronous buffering immediately, even though the scenario has not shown that mechanism is the limiting constraint.
Keep the happy path and treat a read across mixed snapshots as an operational exception that the caller can resolve manually.
Select a named cloud or vendor product first and infer the workload, ownership, and guarantee from that product's defaults.

feedback.Reason: Enforce quotas and overload signaling at the boundary that can identify caller and resource cost. It addresses the report must state its freshness and use a consistent cutoff through an explicit mechanism and keeps a read across mixed snapshots inside a visible ownership and recovery boundary.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Fairness requires an attributable budget and an explicit response when capacity is unavailable. The transfer case makes the enforcement point explicit instead of relying on a product default.
Details.scenarioApplication: For financial reporting, the decision keeps the report must state its freshness and use a consistent cutoff attached to the owner that can observe the state. The design treats a read across mixed snapshots as a named failure path.
Details.errorCorrection: The distractors either make the boundary unowned, add unmeasured complexity, ignore recovery, or replace mechanism reasoning with provider trivia. Transfer the ownership and failure rule, then re-evaluate the changed workload rather than copying a product solution.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Do not reduce “Rate limits, quotas, fairness, and overload signaling” to terminology recall. Distinguish protocol mechanics from domain boundaries; a fashionable API style is not automatically the correct contract. The trade-off is that explicit ownership and evidence may require a narrower contract or an operational signal, but that cost is preferable to silently violating the stated guarantee.
Details.ownership: The service or boundary that owns the relevant state and can enforce rate limits, quotas, fairness, and overload signaling must own the decision; callers coordinate through the contract.
Details.transfer: Carry the ownership and failure rule into a new domain, then re-check the changed workload, guarantee, and recovery requirement.
Details.provenance: Technical claim anchored to RFC 9110 — HTTP Semantics (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html); scenario, options, and feedback are independently authored.
